title: NEET UG 2026 - Set 3: Tricky & Advanced (Topper-Level)
description: 180 challenging MCQs focusing on tricky concepts, common traps, calculation-heavy problems, and assertion-reason type questions. These separate 650+ scorers from 550-range students.

deep_analysis.methodology: Questions targeting common conceptual errors, multi-step calculations, and frequently confused concepts identified from PYQ wrong-answer analysis
tricky_patterns: Confusing similar named reactions in organic chemistry
Assertion-Reason with 'correct but not explanation' trap
Dimensional analysis problems with hidden conversions

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A uniform disc and a uniform ring, both of mass M and radius R, are released from the top of a rough inclined plane. Which reaches the bottom first?
questions.explanation: Acceleration a = g sinθ/(1 + I/MR²). For disc: I = MR²/2, a = 2g sinθ/3. For ring: I = MR², a = g sinθ/2. Disc has greater acceleration → reaches first.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A rod of length L is hinged at one end. The moment of inertia about the hinge is ML²/3. If it falls from horizontal position, the angular velocity when it becomes vertical is:
questions.explanation: Energy conservation: Mg(L/2) = ½Iω². Mg(L/2) = ½(ML²/3)ω². ω = √(3g/L)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two identical metal spheres A and B have charges +4Q and -2Q. They are first brought into contact and then separated. Now sphere B is brought in contact with an uncharged sphere C of same size and separated. The final charge on C is:
questions.explanation: A+B contact: total = 4Q-2Q = 2Q, each gets Q. Now B(Q) touches C(0): total = Q, each gets Q/2. Charge on C = Q/2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A charged particle is released from rest in a uniform electric field. Its kinetic energy after time t is proportional to:
questions.explanation: In uniform E, acceleration a = qE/m (constant). v = at. KE = ½mv² = ½m(at)² ∝ t²

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A metallic ring of radius R is placed perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field B. If the field is suddenly switched off in time Δt, the induced EMF is:
questions.explanation: EMF = -dΦ/dt = -(0 - BπR²)/Δt = BπR²/Δt

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A conducting rod of length l moves with velocity v in a direction perpendicular to a long, straight wire carrying current I. The rod is at distance r from the wire. The EMF induced across the rod is NOT uniform because:
options: The magnetic field is non-uniform (varies as 1/r)
questions.explanation: Magnetic field from a long wire B = μ₀I/2πr varies inversely with distance. Different parts of rod are at different distances → non-uniform EMF distribution.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A fish looking up through water sees the outside world in a circle of radius r. If the refractive index of water is 4/3 and the fish is at depth d, then r equals:
questions.explanation: Critical angle: sin C = 1/μ = 3/4. tan C = sin C/cos C = (3/4)/(√7/4) = 3/√7. r = d tan C = 3d/√7

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In a compound microscope, if the objective and eyepiece are interchanged:
questions.explanation: Objective has short focal length and eyepiece has long focal length. Interchanging gives much lower magnification as M ∝ 1/fo × 1/fe and now the shorter FL lens is eyepiece.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: If the kinetic energy of a photoelectron emitted from a metal surface is doubled, the stopping potential will:
questions.explanation: eV₀ = KE_max. If KE doubles, V₀ = 2KE/e = 2V₀(original). Stopping potential doubles.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The ratio of de Broglie wavelengths of a proton and an alpha particle accelerated through the same potential difference is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An ideal gas undergoes a cyclic process as shown (a triangle on PV diagram with vertices at (P₀,V₀), (2P₀,V₀), and (P₀,2V₀)). The net work done by the gas per cycle is:
questions.explanation: Work = Area of triangle on PV diagram = ½ × base × height = ½ × V₀ × P₀ = P₀V₀/2

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In an adiabatic process for an ideal gas, if the volume is doubled, the temperature changes by factor (γ = 5/3):
questions.explanation: TV^(γ-1) = constant. T₁V₁^(γ-1) = T₂V₂^(γ-1). T₂/T₁ = (V₁/V₂)^(γ-1) = (1/2)^(2/3)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A satellite is revolving around Earth in a circular orbit of radius r. If its orbital velocity is suddenly made zero, the time it takes to fall to Earth's surface (radius R) is approximately: (Assume R << r)
options: T/4√2 where T is orbital period
questions.explanation: When velocity = 0, satellite falls as if in a degenerate ellipse (straight line) with semi-major axis r/2. Time = T'/2 = (T/2√2)/2 = T/(4√2) where T' is period of this orbit.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two SHMs are represented by y₁ = A sin(ωt) and y₂ = A cos(ωt). The ratio of their maximum velocities is:
questions.explanation: v_max = Aω for both (since both have same A and ω). cos(ωt) = sin(ωt + π/2) → same amplitude. Ratio = 1:1

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A uniform wire of resistance 12Ω is bent in the form of a circle. The effective resistance between two diametrically opposite points is:
questions.explanation: Wire bent into circle creates two 6Ω semicircles in parallel between diametrically opposite points. R = 6×6/(6+6) = 3Ω

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In a Zener diode voltage regulator, if the input voltage increases, the current through the Zener diode:
questions.explanation: In Zener regulator, V_out = V_Z (constant). If V_in increases, extra current flows through Zener to maintain constant output voltage. I_Z increases.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In single slit diffraction, if the slit width is equal to the wavelength of light, the angular width of the central maximum is:
questions.explanation: First minimum: sin θ = λ/a = λ/λ = 1, θ = 90°. Angular width of central max = 2×90° = 180° (light spreads over entire forward hemisphere).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A current-carrying loop is placed in a uniform magnetic field. The torque on it is maximum when the angle between the area vector and field is:
questions.explanation: τ = M × B = MB sinθ. Maximum when θ = 90° (area vector perpendicular to B). Note: NOT when plane is perpendicular to B.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A body is projected at angle θ with the horizontal. The velocity at the highest point makes angle φ with the horizontal. Then φ equals:
questions.explanation: At highest point, vertical component = 0. Only horizontal component u cosθ remains. Velocity is entirely horizontal → φ = 0°.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A body weighs 72 N in air and 60 N in water. Its relative density is:
questions.explanation: Buoyant force = 72-60 = 12N = weight of water displaced. RD = weight in air/buoyant force = 72/12 = 6

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two point charges +q and +4q are placed 6 cm apart. The point on the line joining them where electric field is zero is:
questions.explanation: E=0 between charges (both positive). kq/x² = k(4q)/(6-x)². (6-x)² = 4x². 6-x = 2x (taking +ve root). x = 2 cm from +q.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two tuning forks A and B produce 4 beats per second. On loading A with wax, beats become 2 per second. If the frequency of B is 256 Hz, the original frequency of A is:
questions.explanation: A - B = ±4. Loading A decreases its frequency. If A = 260, after loading A decreases → comes closer to 256 → beats decrease to 2. Correct! A = 260 Hz.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A spring of force constant k is cut into three equal parts. The force constant of each part is:
questions.explanation: When spring is cut into n equal parts, each part has force constant nk. Here n=3, so each part has constant 3k.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In the nuclear reaction ²³⁸U → ²⁰⁶Pb + x(⁴He) + y(β⁻), the values of x and y are:
questions.explanation: Mass: 238 = 206 + 4x → x = 8. Charge: 92 = 82 + 2(8) - y → y = 6. (8 alpha + 6 beta emissions)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A monkey of mass 40 kg climbs on a rope that can withstand a maximum tension of 600 N. The maximum acceleration with which the monkey can climb up is: (g = 10 m/s²)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The work done in moving a charge of 5μC from one point to another in an equipotential surface is:
questions.explanation: On an equipotential surface, potential difference = 0. W = qΔV = q × 0 = 0. No work is done regardless of path.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A 4μF capacitor is charged to 100V and a 6μF capacitor is charged to 150V. They are connected positive plate to positive plate. The common potential is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The phase difference between voltage and current in a pure inductive circuit is:
questions.explanation: In pure inductor: V = L di/dt. For I = I₀sinωt, V = LωI₀cosωt = V₀sin(ωt+π/2). Voltage leads current by 90°.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The total number of spectral lines emitted when electrons in hydrogen atoms de-excite from n=4 to ground state is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A ray of light passes from a denser medium (μ=√2) to a rarer medium. The angle of incidence is 45°. The angle of refraction is:
questions.explanation: sin r = μ sin i = √2 × sin 45° = √2 × (1/√2) = 1. r = 90°. This is the critical angle condition → ray grazes the surface.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The electric field at the centre of a uniformly charged ring of charge Q and radius R is:
questions.explanation: By symmetry, the electric field contributions from diametrically opposite charge elements cancel out at the centre. E = 0.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Inside a uniform spherical shell, the gravitational field is:
questions.explanation: Shell theorem: gravitational field inside a uniform spherical shell is zero everywhere (contributions cancel by symmetry).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Five equal resistors each of value R are connected as shown (forming a Wheatstone bridge with one in the galvanometer arm). The equivalent resistance between two opposite corners is:
questions.explanation: In balanced Wheatstone bridge, the middle resistor carries no current. Equivalent = (2R × 2R)/(2R + 2R) = R. But with unbalanced bridge with R in middle, using Y-Δ or symmetry: R_eq = R.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The speed of electromagnetic wave in a medium of dielectric constant 4 and relative permeability 1 is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: If force (F), velocity (v), and time (T) are taken as fundamental quantities, the dimensions of mass are:
questions.explanation: F = ma = m(v/T). m = FT/v = FV⁻¹T

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A wire of length L and area A is stretched by ΔL. If Young's modulus is Y, the energy stored per unit volume is:
questions.explanation: Energy/volume = ½ × stress × strain = ½ × Y × strain × strain = ½Y(ΔL/L)²

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two parallel wires carry currents in the same direction. The force between them is:
questions.explanation: Parallel currents in same direction attract each other. This is because each wire's field exerts a force toward the other wire.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A car of mass 1000 kg moves on a banked road of radius 100 m. If the banking angle is 30°, the speed for which no friction is needed is: (g=10 m/s²)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two identical rods, one of copper and other of steel, are connected in series and their free ends are maintained at 100°C and 0°C. If thermal conductivity of copper is 9 times that of steel, the junction temperature is:
questions.explanation: In series, heat flow is same. K₁A(100-T)/L = K₂A(T-0)/L. 9K(100-T) = K×T. 900-9T = T. 10T = 900. T = 90°C

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The number of photoelectrons emitted is proportional to:
questions.explanation: Number of photoelectrons ∝ number of photons ∝ intensity (for frequency above threshold). KE depends on frequency, not number.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A parallel plate capacitor with air has capacitance C. If half the space between plates is filled with a dielectric of constant K, the new capacitance is:
questions.explanation: If dielectric fills half the space (side by side - parallel): C_new = C/2 + KC/2 = C(1+K)/2

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In a common emitter transistor amplifier, the current gain β = 50. If the collector resistance is 5 kΩ and input resistance is 500 Ω, the voltage gain is:
questions.explanation: Voltage gain = β × R_C/R_in = 50 × 5000/500 = 500

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In Young's experiment, the ratio of maximum to minimum intensity is 9:1. The ratio of amplitudes of the two interfering waves is:
questions.explanation: I_max/I_min = (a₁+a₂)²/(a₁-a₂)² = 9/1. (a₁+a₂)/(a₁-a₂) = 3. a₁+a₂ = 3a₁-3a₂. 4a₂ = 2a₁. a₁/a₂ = 2/1

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The percentage error in the measurement of the volume of a sphere if the percentage error in measuring the radius is 1% is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A bar magnet of magnetic moment M is cut into two equal halves along its length. The magnetic moment of each half is:
questions.explanation: Cut along length: pole strength halves, length same. m' = m/2, l' = l. M' = m'l' = (m/2)l = M/2

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: For a first-order reaction A → B, if [A] reduces from 0.1 M to 0.025 M in 40 minutes, the half-life of the reaction is:
questions.explanation: 0.1 → 0.05 (one t₁/₂) → 0.025 (two t₁/₂). Two half-lives = 40 min. t₁/₂ = 20 minutes.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: For the reaction 2N₂O₅ → 4NO₂ + O₂, if the rate of formation of NO₂ is 2.8×10⁻³ mol/L/s, the rate of disappearance of N₂O₅ is:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The number of faradays required to deposit 1 mole of aluminium from Al₂O₃ is:
questions.explanation: Al³⁺ + 3e⁻ → Al. 1 mole Al requires 3 moles of electrons = 3 Faradays.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: [Cr(NH₃)₆]³⁺ is coloured because of:
questions.explanation: Cr³⁺ (d³) in octahedral field has unpaired d electrons. d-d transition absorbs visible light → complementary color appears.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The correct order of stability of conformations of ethane is:
questions.explanation: Staggered conformation is most stable (dihedral angle 60°, minimum torsional strain). Eclipsed (0°) is least stable.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Kolbe's electrolysis of sodium acetate gives:
questions.explanation: Kolbe's electrolysis: 2CH₃COONa → CH₃-CH₃ + 2CO₂ + 2Na (at anode: 2CH₃COO⁻ → C₂H₆ + 2CO₂ + 2e⁻)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Cannizzaro reaction is given by aldehydes which:
questions.explanation: Cannizzaro reaction (disproportionation) is given by aldehydes without α-H (like HCHO, C₆H₅CHO). Aldehydes with α-H give aldol condensation instead.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Van't Hoff factor for 0.1 M Ba(NO₃)₂ solution (assuming complete dissociation) is:
questions.explanation: Ba(NO₃)₂ → Ba²⁺ + 2NO₃⁻ (3 particles from 1). Van't Hoff factor i = 3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A solution of urea in water has boiling point of 100.18°C. The molality of solution is: (Kb for water = 0.52 K/m)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In a face-centered cubic crystal, the coordination number is:
questions.explanation: In FCC, each atom is surrounded by 12 nearest neighbours (4 in same plane, 4 above, 4 below). Coordination number = 12.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which noble gas compound was first prepared?
questions.explanation: Neil Bartlett (1962) prepared the first noble gas compound Xe+[PtF₆]⁻ by reacting xenon with PtF₆.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: For the process: H₂O(l) → H₂O(g) at 100°C and 1 atm, which is correct?
questions.explanation: At boiling point (equilibrium), ΔG = 0. The process is reversible at this temperature and pressure.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The molecule with maximum dipole moment among the following is:
questions.explanation: HF has the highest dipole moment (1.91 D) due to the highest electronegativity difference between H and F, despite shorter bond length.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following shows maximum number of oxidation states?
questions.explanation: Mn (Z=25, [Ar]3d⁵4s²) shows oxidation states from +2 to +7, the maximum among transition elements (7 oxidation states).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The conjugate base of H₂PO₄⁻ is:
questions.explanation: Conjugate base = species formed after losing one proton. H₂PO₄⁻ → HPO₄²⁻ + H⁺

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Among CH₃OH, C₂H₅OH, C₃H₇OH, and C₄H₉OH, which has the highest boiling point?
questions.explanation: Boiling point increases with molecular weight in homologous series. C₄H₉OH (butanol) has highest molecular weight → highest BP.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The IUPAC name of CH₃-CO-CH₂-CH₂-CH₃ is:
questions.explanation: 5-carbon chain with ketone at C-2. IUPAC: Pentan-2-one (numbering from the end closer to carbonyl group).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In a concentration cell, EMF is zero when:
options: Concentrations of both half-cells are equal
questions.explanation: Concentration cell: EMF = (RT/nF)ln(C₁/C₂). When C₁ = C₂, ln(1) = 0, EMF = 0.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Physical adsorption is characterized by:
options: Low enthalpy of adsorption (20-40 kJ/mol), reversible, multi-layer
questions.explanation: Physisorption: low enthalpy (van der Waals forces), reversible, not specific, multi-layer, decreases with temperature increase.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Bakelite is obtained by the polymerization of phenol with:
questions.explanation: Bakelite = phenol + formaldehyde (condensation polymer). Cross-linked, thermosetting plastic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following will undergo racemization in SN1 reaction?
options: A chiral substrate (optically active) gives mixture of R and S
A substrate with no leaving group
questions.explanation: SN1 proceeds via planar carbocation intermediate. Nucleophile attacks from both sides → racemic mixture (retention + inversion).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The orbital angular momentum of an electron in 2s orbital is:
questions.explanation: Orbital angular momentum = √(l(l+1))ℏ. For s orbital, l = 0. L = √(0×1)ℏ = 0.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Markovnikov's rule predicts the major product of HBr addition to propene as:
questions.explanation: Markovnikov: H adds to C with more H's. CH₃CH=CH₂ + HBr → CH₃CHBrCH₃ (2-bromopropane is major product).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The number of lone pairs on the central atom in ICl₂⁻ is:
questions.explanation: ICl₂⁻: I has 7 + 1(charge) = 8 electrons around it. 2 bond pairs + 3 lone pairs = 5 pairs total. sp³d hybridization, linear shape.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: If Kp for N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ is K, then Kp for ½N₂ + 3/2H₂ ⇌ NH₃ is:
questions.explanation: When equation is halved, Kp becomes square root. Kp(new) = Kp(original)^(1/2) = √K

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Williamson synthesis is used to prepare:
questions.explanation: Williamson synthesis: R-O⁻Na⁺ + R'-X → R-O-R' + NaX. It's used to prepare symmetrical and unsymmetrical ethers.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the thermite process, the reducing agent used is:
questions.explanation: Thermite process: Fe₂O₃ + 2Al → Al₂O₃ + 2Fe. Al is the reducing agent (highly reactive metal).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The product of ozonolysis of but-2-ene is:
questions.explanation: CH₃CH=CHCH₃ + O₃ → CH₃CHO + CH₃CHO (2 moles of acetaldehyde). Each C=C bond gives two carbonyl compounds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The correct decreasing order of bond angle is:
options: H₂O < NH₃ < CH₄ is WRONG; correct is CH₄ > NH₃ > H₂O
questions.explanation: Bond angle: CH₄ (109.5°) > NH₃ (107°) > H₂O (104.5°). Lone pairs reduce bond angle (lp-bp repulsion > bp-bp).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Clemmensen reduction converts a carbonyl group to:
questions.explanation: Clemmensen reduction: >C=O → >CH₂ using Zn-Hg/HCl. Reduces ketones/aldehydes to hydrocarbons.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The solubility product of BaSO₄ is 1.5×10⁻⁹. The solubility (in mol/L) is:
questions.explanation: BaSO₄ → Ba²⁺ + SO₄²⁻. Ksp = s² = 1.5×10⁻⁹. s = √(1.5×10⁻⁹) = 3.87×10⁻⁵ mol/L

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Schottky defect leads to:
questions.explanation: Schottky defect: equal number of cations and anions are missing from lattice → vacant sites → density decreases.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is used to prepare:
questions.explanation: Gabriel synthesis gives only primary amines. Potassium phthalimide + R-X → N-alkylphthalimide → hydrolysis → R-NH₂.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the reaction: MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5e⁻ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O, the equivalent weight of KMnO₄ is:
questions.explanation: Mn goes from +7 to +2 (gain of 5 electrons). n-factor = 5. Equivalent weight = Molecular weight/5 = 158/5 = 31.6

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Carbylamine reaction is a test for:
questions.explanation: Carbylamine (isocyanide) test: R-NH₂ + CHCl₃ + 3KOH → R-NC + 3KCl + 3H₂O. Only primary amines give this test.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The correct CFSE (Crystal Field Stabilization Energy) for d⁶ low spin octahedral complex is:
questions.explanation: d⁶ low spin: t₂g⁶ eg⁰. CFSE = -6(4Dq) + 0(6Dq) = -24Dq. Pairing energy = 2P (for 2 extra pairings beyond d⁶ free ion). Net = -24Dq + 2P.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Reverse osmosis is used for:
questions.explanation: Reverse osmosis applies pressure greater than osmotic pressure to force water through semi-permeable membrane → desalination.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The monomer of natural rubber is:
questions.explanation: Natural rubber is cis-1,4-polyisoprene. Monomer: isoprene (CH₂=C(CH₃)-CH=CH₂)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which test distinguishes between methanol and ethanol?
questions.explanation: Iodoform test: Ethanol (CH₃CH₂OH) gives iodoform (CHI₃) due to CH₃-CHOH group. Methanol lacks this group → negative test.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The element with highest ionization enthalpy is:
questions.explanation: Helium has the highest first ionization enthalpy (2372 kJ/mol) due to very small size, high nuclear charge, and stable 1s² configuration.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: For an isolated system (no heat exchange), if entropy change (ΔS) > 0, the process is:
questions.explanation: For isolated system: ΔS > 0 (irreversible, spontaneous), ΔS = 0 (reversible/equilibrium), ΔS < 0 (impossible).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Chlorine water is both an oxidizing and bleaching agent because it contains:
questions.explanation: Cl₂ + H₂O → HOCl + HCl. HOCl → HCl + [O]. Nascent oxygen oxidizes colored substances → bleaching action.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The Hinsberg test is used to distinguish between:
questions.explanation: Hinsberg test (benzenesulfonyl chloride): 1° amine → soluble in NaOH; 2° amine → insoluble; 3° amine → no reaction initially.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Among NF₃, BF₃, and ClF₃, the molecule with zero dipole moment is:
questions.explanation: BF₃ is trigonal planar (sp²) → symmetrical → dipole moment = 0. NF₃ is pyramidal, ClF₃ is T-shaped (both non-zero dipole).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Sandmeyer's reaction converts a diazonium salt to:
options: Aryl halide (Cl or Br) using Cu₂Cl₂/Cu₂Br₂
questions.explanation: Sandmeyer: ArN₂⁺ + CuCl/CuBr → ArCl/ArBr + N₂. Replaces N₂⁺ with Cl/Br using cuprous salts as catalyst.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a pedigree chart, an autosomal recessive trait typically shows that:
options: Affected individuals often have unaffected parents (carriers)
All children of affected parents are affected
questions.explanation: Autosomal recessive: appears to skip generations, affected have carrier parents (Aa × Aa → aa), both sexes equally affected.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: If a gene pair Aa undergoes non-disjunction during meiosis II, the resulting gametes will be:
options: AA, O, a, a (or Aa, O, A, a depending on which cell)
questions.explanation: Non-disjunction in meiosis II: one cell fails to separate chromatids. Results in 2 cells with extra chromosome, and one with none (nullisomic gamete O).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The Wobble hypothesis explains why:
options: The genetic code is degenerate (multiple codons for one amino acid)
questions.explanation: Wobble hypothesis (Crick): 3rd position of codon can pair with non-standard bases on tRNA anticodon → one tRNA reads multiple codons → explains degeneracy.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In eukaryotes, the mRNA undergoes processing including all EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Shine-Dalgarno sequence is in PROKARYOTIC mRNA (ribosome binding). Eukaryotic mRNA processing: 5' cap + 3' poly-A tail + splicing.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The relationship between tiger and deer is an example of:
questions.explanation: Predation: tiger benefits (+) by eating deer, deer is harmed (-). It's a +/- interaction.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: r-selected species are characterized by:
options: Small size, early maturity, many offspring, short lifespan
Large size, late maturity, few offspring
questions.explanation: r-selected: rapid reproduction, many offspring, small size, early maturity, short lifespan (e.g., insects, bacteria). Opportunistic colonizers.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT membrane-bound?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are NOT membrane-bound organelles. They are composed of rRNA and proteins, found free in cytoplasm or attached to RER.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The fluid mosaic model of cell membrane was proposed by:
questions.explanation: Singer and Nicolson (1972) proposed the fluid mosaic model: lipid bilayer with integral and peripheral proteins floating in it.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The blood vessel that carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart is:
questions.explanation: Pulmonary veins carry oxygenated blood from lungs to left atrium. (Exception: pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from heart to lungs.)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The bundle of His and Purkinje fibres are part of the:
questions.explanation: Bundle of His and Purkinje fibres are specialized cardiac muscle cells forming the cardiac conduction system for coordinated heartbeat.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Heparin is an anticoagulant produced by:
questions.explanation: Heparin is produced by mast cells and basophils. It prevents clotting by inhibiting thrombin and other clotting factors.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The oxygen evolved during photosynthesis comes from:
questions.explanation: Proved by Ruben and Kamen using O¹⁸ labeled water: O₂ released comes entirely from photolysis of water (Hill reaction).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Photorespiration occurs in C₃ plants because RuBisCO also fixes:
questions.explanation: RuBisCO has dual activity: carboxylase (fixes CO₂) and oxygenase (fixes O₂). O₂ fixation leads to photorespiration (wasteful, no ATP produced).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The Ti plasmid is used in genetic engineering of plants. Ti stands for:
questions.explanation: Ti plasmid (Tumor inducing) from Agrobacterium tumefaciens. Its T-DNA integrates into plant genome. Modified Ti plasmids used as vectors.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In gel electrophoresis, DNA fragments move towards the:
questions.explanation: DNA is negatively charged (phosphate groups). It moves towards anode (+ve electrode). Smaller fragments move faster.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Endosperm in angiosperms is:
questions.explanation: Endosperm formed by triple fusion: 2 polar nuclei (n+n) + 1 sperm (n) → Primary Endosperm Nucleus (3n) → endosperm is triploid.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The part of the flower that develops into fruit is:
questions.explanation: After fertilization, ovary develops into fruit. Ovary wall → pericarp. Ovules → seeds.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which phylum shows 'tube within a tube' body plan?
questions.explanation: Aschelminthes (roundworms) have a complete digestive tract (separate mouth and anus) → 'tube within a tube' arrangement.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The wings of birds and wings of insects are examples of:
questions.explanation: Bird wings (modified forelimbs) and insect wings (exoskeletal extensions) have different origins but same function → analogous (convergent evolution).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: According to Oparin's theory, the first life forms were:
questions.explanation: First life: chemoheterotrophs (obtained energy from chemical reactions, used organic molecules from primordial soup as food).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which cells are attacked by HIV?
questions.explanation: HIV specifically attacks Helper T-lymphocytes (CD4+ cells), macrophages. Destroys immune system → AIDS.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Interferon is:
options: An antiviral protein produced by virus-infected cells
questions.explanation: Interferons are proteins secreted by virus-infected cells that protect neighbouring uninfected cells from viral infection (innate immunity).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Casparian strips are found in:
questions.explanation: Casparian strips (suberin bands) in endodermal cell walls of roots prevent apoplastic water movement → force symplastic pathway.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Open vascular bundles are found in:
questions.explanation: Open vascular bundles (with cambium between xylem and phloem) are in dicot stems → allows secondary growth. Monocot bundles are closed.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: If a cell has 20 chromosomes at G1 phase, how many chromatids will be present at metaphase of mitosis?
questions.explanation: After S phase, each chromosome has 2 chromatids. At metaphase: 20 chromosomes × 2 chromatids = 40 chromatids.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Bivalent formation occurs during:
questions.explanation: Bivalent (homologous pair) formation occurs during zygotene by the process of synapsis (synaptonemal complex formation).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Juxtaglomerular apparatus is formed by:
options: Loop of Henle and collecting duct
questions.explanation: JGA = JG cells (modified smooth muscle of afferent arteriole) + Macula densa (modified cells of DCT). Secretes renin.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the sliding filament theory of muscle contraction, which of the following remains unchanged?
questions.explanation: During contraction: A-band (dark band containing myosin) remains SAME length. I-band and H-zone decrease. Sarcomere shortens.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Nonsense codons (stop codons) are:
questions.explanation: Stop codons: UAA (ochre), UAG (amber), UGA (opal). They don't code for any amino acid → signal termination of translation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The process of removal of introns and joining of exons is called:
questions.explanation: RNA splicing: removal of introns (non-coding) and joining of exons (coding sequences) by spliceosomes (snRNPs) in eukaryotes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which biogeochemical cycle does NOT have a gaseous phase?
questions.explanation: Phosphorus cycle is purely sedimentary (no gaseous phase). It cycles through rocks → soil → organisms → water → sediments.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The maximum growth rate of a population under ideal conditions is called:
questions.explanation: Biotic potential (intrinsic rate of natural increase, r_max) is the maximum reproductive capacity under ideal unlimited conditions.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is a C₄ plant?
questions.explanation: Sugarcane is a C₄ plant (also maize, sorghum). Wheat, rice, potato are C₃ plants. C₄ plants have Kranz anatomy and PEP carboxylase.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Vernalization requires exposure to:
questions.explanation: Vernalization: exposure to low temperature (0-5°C) for a certain period to induce flowering (e.g., wheat, rye). Perceived at meristem.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The selectable marker in pBR322 that helps identify recombinants through insertional inactivation is:
questions.explanation: Foreign DNA insertion into ampR or tetR gene inactivates it. Recombinants lose resistance to that antibiotic → identified by replica plating.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Passive immunity is acquired by:
questions.explanation: Passive immunity: ready-made antibodies transferred (mother→fetus via placenta, colostrum, or injection of antiserum). No memory cells formed.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Amniocentesis is used to detect:
questions.explanation: Amniocentesis: amniotic fluid sample analyzed for chromosomal abnormalities, genetic disorders, and sex determination of fetus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Epistasis where one gene masks the expression of another gene at a different locus gives a modified ratio of:
questions.explanation: Epistasis modifies 9:3:3:1 ratio. Dominant epistasis → 12:3:1, Recessive epistasis → 9:3:4, Complementary → 9:7, Duplicate → 15:1.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The phenomenon where a single gene influences multiple phenotypic traits is called:
questions.explanation: Pleiotropy: one gene affects multiple characters (e.g., sickle cell gene affects RBC shape, oxygen transport, spleen, etc.).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Facilitated diffusion differs from active transport in that it:
questions.explanation: Facilitated diffusion: along concentration gradient, no ATP needed, requires carrier/channel proteins. Active transport: against gradient, needs ATP.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The part of the brain that controls involuntary actions like heart rate and breathing is:
questions.explanation: Medulla oblongata (brain stem) controls vital involuntary functions: cardiac center, respiratory center, vasomotor center.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The hormone responsible for basal metabolic rate regulation is:
questions.explanation: T₃ and T₄ from thyroid gland regulate BMR. Hyperthyroidism → high BMR; Hypothyroidism → low BMR.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The pioneer species in hydrarch succession (in water bodies) is:
questions.explanation: Hydrarch succession (aquatic): Pioneer = phytoplankton → submerged → floating → reed swamp → woodland → climax forest. Lichens are pioneers in xerosere.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: End products of light reaction of photosynthesis are:
questions.explanation: Light reactions produce: ATP (photophosphorylation), NADPH (from NADP+ reduction), and O₂ (from water photolysis).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the 7-celled embryo sac, the cells present are:
options: 3 antipodals + 2 synergids + 1 egg + 1 central cell (with 2 polar nuclei)
questions.explanation: 7-celled, 8-nucleate embryo sac: egg apparatus (1 egg + 2 synergids) + 3 antipodals + 1 large central cell (2 polar nuclei).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Hershey and Chase experiment proved that:
options: Both DNA and protein are genetic material
questions.explanation: Hershey-Chase (1952) used T2 bacteriophage with ³²P-labeled DNA and ³⁵S-labeled protein. ³²P entered bacteria → DNA is genetic material.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The Lac operon is an example of:
questions.explanation: Lac operon: normally repressed (repressor binds operator → negative control). Induced by lactose/allolactose → inducible. Hence negative inducible.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is the correct sequence of evolution of man?
options: Australopithecus → Homo habilis → Homo erectus → Homo sapiens
Homo sapiens → Homo erectus → Homo habilis
questions.explanation: Human evolution: Dryopithecus → Ramapithecus → Australopithecus → H. habilis → H. erectus → H. neanderthalensis → H. sapiens.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Addison's disease is caused by:
questions.explanation: Addison's disease: deficiency of adrenal cortex hormones (cortisol, aldosterone). Symptoms: weakness, low BP, darkening of skin.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The contraceptive method that also prevents STDs is:
questions.explanation: Condoms (male/female) are the only contraceptive that also prevents STDs by providing a physical barrier against pathogens.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: RNA interference (RNAi) involves:
options: Silencing of specific mRNA by complementary dsRNA
questions.explanation: RNAi: double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) → processed by Dicer → siRNA → binds to complementary mRNA → silences gene expression.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The gametophyte is the dominant phase in the life cycle of:
questions.explanation: In bryophytes, the gametophyte (n) is the dominant, independent, photosynthetic phase. Sporophyte is dependent on gametophyte.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: ATP synthesis in mitochondria occurs by:
questions.explanation: Oxidative phosphorylation: ETC creates proton gradient across inner mitochondrial membrane → protons flow through ATP synthase → ATP (chemiosmotic theory by Peter Mitchell).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone System (RAAS) is activated when:
options: Blood pressure falls / blood volume decreases
questions.explanation: Low BP/volume → JG cells release renin → angiotensinogen → angiotensin I → ACE → angiotensin II → aldosterone → Na⁺/water retention → BP rises.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In stratospheric ozone depletion, the catalyst responsible is:
questions.explanation: CFCs release Cl atoms in stratosphere. Cl + O₃ → ClO + O₂, ClO + O → Cl + O₂. One Cl destroys thousands of O₃ molecules catalytically.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The net equation for aerobic respiration is:
questions.explanation: Aerobic respiration: glucose + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O + energy (36-38 ATP). Occurs in cytoplasm (glycolysis) and mitochondria (Krebs + ETC).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In incomplete dominance, the F₂ phenotypic ratio is:
questions.explanation: Incomplete dominance: heterozygote shows intermediate phenotype. F₂: 1 red : 2 pink : 1 white = 1:2:1 (phenotypic = genotypic ratio).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The enzyme reverse transcriptase is found in:
questions.explanation: Reverse transcriptase (RNA-dependent DNA polymerase) is found in retroviruses. It converts viral RNA → DNA (reverse of central dogma).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which part of nephron is impermeable to water?
questions.explanation: Ascending limb of loop of Henle is impermeable to water but permeable to NaCl (active transport out). This creates the medullary concentration gradient.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The term 'ecosystem' was coined by:
questions.explanation: Arthur George Tansley coined the term 'ecosystem' in 1935, defining it as the interacting system of living organisms and physical environment.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Polyembryony is commonly seen in:
questions.explanation: Polyembryony (multiple embryos in one seed) is common in Citrus due to nucellar embryos developing alongside zygotic embryo.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Turner's syndrome has the karyotype:
questions.explanation: Turner's syndrome: 45, XO (monosomic for X). Features: female, short stature, webbed neck, infertile. Klinefelter's = 47, XXY.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Peroxisomes contain the enzyme:
questions.explanation: Peroxisomes contain catalase (breaks down H₂O₂ → H₂O + O₂) and oxidases. Important in fatty acid β-oxidation and photorespiration.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Long-day plants flower when the critical dark period is:
questions.explanation: Long-day plants (actually short-night plants) flower when dark period is LESS than the critical duration. Phytochrome Pfr promotes flowering.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: CSF (Cerebrospinal fluid) is secreted by:
questions.explanation: CSF is secreted by choroid plexus (vascular tissue) in the ventricles of the brain. It cushions brain and spinal cord.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Telomerase is a:
options: Reverse transcriptase that adds repetitive sequences to telomeres
questions.explanation: Telomerase is a ribonucleoprotein (has RNA template) that adds TTAGGG repeats to telomeres, preventing chromosome shortening. Active in cancer cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The gland that acts as both endocrine and exocrine is:
questions.explanation: Pancreas: endocrine (islets of Langerhans → insulin, glucagon) + exocrine (acinar cells → pancreatic juice with digestive enzymes).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The niche overlap between two competing species typically leads to:
questions.explanation: Gause's competitive exclusion: two species with identical niche cannot coexist. Either one excludes other, or they evolve resource partitioning.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Transgenic animals are those which have:
options: Foreign gene integrated in their genome
questions.explanation: Transgenic animals have a foreign gene (transgene) artificially inserted into their genome using rDNA technology (e.g., transgenic mice, Rosie the cow).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Double fertilization and triple fusion are events unique to:
questions.explanation: Double fertilization (syngamy + triple fusion) is unique to angiosperms. Not found in any other plant group.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Blood calcium level is regulated by:
questions.explanation: PTH (from parathyroid) increases blood Ca²⁺. TCT/Calcitonin (from thyroid C-cells) decreases blood Ca²⁺. They work antagonistically.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Colchicine prevents cell division by:
questions.explanation: Colchicine binds to tubulin proteins, preventing microtubule assembly → no spindle formation → cell arrested at metaphase. Used to produce polyploidy.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The Q₁₀ (temperature coefficient) for enzyme-catalyzed reactions is typically:
questions.explanation: Q₁₀ = 2-3 for enzymatic reactions (rate doubles or triples for every 10°C rise). Only valid up to optimum temperature.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The number of Barr bodies in a cell with XXXXY karyotype is:
questions.explanation: Barr bodies = number of X chromosomes - 1. XXXXY has 4 X chromosomes. Barr bodies = 4 - 1 = 3.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Detritivores differ from decomposers in that they:
questions.explanation: Detritivores (earthworms, crabs) ingest and internally digest detritus. Decomposers (bacteria, fungi) secrete enzymes externally and absorb nutrients.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Type II diabetes is characterized by:
options: Insulin resistance (target cells don't respond to insulin)
questions.explanation: Type II diabetes (NIDDM): insulin IS produced but target cells are resistant to it. Often associated with obesity and age. Type I = no insulin production.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The suspensor in a developing embryo helps in:
options: Absorbing nutrients from endosperm for the embryo
questions.explanation: Suspensor pushes the developing embryo into the endosperm and helps in nutrient absorption. It's at the micropylar end.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Satellite DNA is useful in:
questions.explanation: Satellite DNA (highly repetitive, non-coding) shows high polymorphism between individuals → basis of DNA fingerprinting (VNTR analysis).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The contractile vacuole in Amoeba is primarily for:
questions.explanation: Contractile vacuole: osmoregulation in freshwater protists. Expels excess water that enters by osmosis (hypotonic environment).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Genetic drift is more significant in:
questions.explanation: Genetic drift: random changes in allele frequency. Effect is pronounced in small populations (sampling error is larger). Can lead to fixation/loss of alleles.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: DPT vaccine provides immunity against:
questions.explanation: DPT vaccine: Diphtheria (Corynebacterium), Pertussis/Whooping cough (Bordetella), Tetanus (Clostridium tetani).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The mineral ion that is required for water splitting during photosynthesis is:
questions.explanation: Mn²⁺ is part of the Oxygen Evolving Complex (OEC/Water Splitting Complex) in PS II. It helps in photolysis: 2H₂O → 4H⁺ + O₂ + 4e⁻.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Net Primary Productivity (NPP) is calculated as:
questions.explanation: NPP = GPP - R (respiration). NPP is the biomass available to consumers. GPP is total photosynthetic production.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The organisms with 'incomplete digestive system' (only one opening) belong to phylum:
questions.explanation: Platyhelminthes (flatworms) have incomplete digestive system with only one opening (mouth = anus). Aschelminthes onward have complete gut.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The condition of having excess urea in blood is called:
questions.explanation: Uremia: excess urea in blood due to kidney failure. Glycosuria = glucose in urine. Ketonuria = ketones in urine.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In DNA, the percentage of adenine is 20%. The percentage of guanine will be:
questions.explanation: Chargaff's rule: A=T, G=C. If A=20%, T=20%. A+T=40%. G+C=60%. G=C=30%.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Vessels are absent in the xylem of:
questions.explanation: Gymnosperms lack vessels (have only tracheids) except Gnetales (Gnetum, Ephedra, Welwitschia). Angiosperms have both vessels and tracheids.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Parthenocarpy refers to:
questions.explanation: Parthenocarpy: fruit formation without fertilization → seedless fruits (e.g., banana, grapes). Can be induced by auxin/gibberellin.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The first genetically modified organism used for commercial insulin production was:
questions.explanation: Humulin (human insulin) was first produced in E. coli (1983) by Eli Lilly. Human insulin gene inserted into E. coli plasmid.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Saltatory conduction occurs in:
questions.explanation: Saltatory conduction: impulse jumps from one Node of Ranvier to next in myelinated neurons. Much faster than continuous conduction in unmyelinated fibres.
